overlaps.detail: Both descriptions discuss turning an explicit orthonormal family with a completeness proof into a HilbertBasis and retaining its element-level identity. This is a shared assembly substep, not an overlap of Hermite completeness with Peter-Weyl density. The OrthogonalL2Bases README presents B2 as a polynomial-facing bridge on R. At Tau Ceti pin f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369, WeightedOrthogonalBasis.lean is broader in its measurable domain, but its input remains f : Nat -> alpha -> R and the output remains Nat-indexed, even when its real values are lifted to complex scalars. CompactGroups uses genuinely complex matrix coefficients indexed by a chosen irreducible-representation skeleton and two finite matrix indices. Its Layer 5 already names the general Mathlib constructor, so this is a scope/citation clarification rather than evidence that Peter-Weyl is blocked on extending B2.
overlaps.proposal: Keep the weighted-system interface and normalization identities in OrthogonalL2Bases B2. In CompactGroups, make the final assembly import explicitly Mathlib HilbertBasis.mkOfOrthogonalEqBot and HilbertBasis.coe_mkOfOrthogonalEqBot, verified at pin 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174 in Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/l2Space.lean, lines 533-563. Retain the OrthogonalL2Bases citation as an element-level API design precedent, not as a claim that its Nat-indexed real-valued bridge accepts arbitrary complex matrix coefficients unchanged. CompactGroups continues to own Schur orthogonality, the irreducible skeleton, the non-circular density proof and the explicit basis-vector identity. Do not merge roadmaps, generalize B2 merely for this consumer, or add an unqualified B2-to-Peter-Weyl prerequisite edge.
